description: Surrogate key, one row per item per day.
Trading day; joins to calendar.date_id.
Menu item sold; joins to menu_items.item_id.

Point-of-sale SKU as printed on the owner's export. Not a key — use item_id. 99% are clean 5-digit codes, but 13 items carry malformed repeated-digit values (e.g. 1064144444) and 6 are 0. Kept as-is: the owner's file is ground truth.
Menu section, e.g. MAKI ROLLS. Spelling varies by row — inconsistent labelling is reproduced, not scrubbed.
Units of this item sold that day. Mean 1.41, 75% are exactly 1, max 16; drawn from a Negative-Binomial so the count is overdispersed.
Menu price per unit at time of sale.
unit_price x quantity_sold, before discount.
Peso value discounted. Applied on ~26% of lines at a median ~7% of gross (Bernoulli x Beta).
gross_sales minus discount. Zero or negative on management comps.
EMPTY ON EVERY ROW. The owner's POS never populated it, so gross profit cannot be derived from this table. Kept empty deliberately.
Tax charged; zero on all but ~0.4% of lines.
dine-in or GrabFood. Delivery share was high in 2021 and decays toward a tenth of trade by 2026.
True where the line was comped (MANAGEMENT category, net <= 0). About 5% of rows.
Surrogate key, one row per ingredient per day.
Stock day; joins to calendar.date_id.
Joins to ingredients.ingredient_id.
Supplier this line is normally bought from; joins to suppliers.supplier_id.
On hand at the start of the day.
Delivered that day, after the supplier's lead time; short-shipped when the fill rate misses.
Drawn by the dishes actually sold: the sum over dishes of units sold x recipe quantity. Equals recipe-implied demand exactly unless stock ran out.
Total discarded that day; itemised in waste.csv.
On hand at end of day. The ledger balances: closing = opening + received - consumed - wasted.
Reorder point s = mean lead-time demand + z x sd, with z = 1.41 (~92% service level).
Placed that day, rounded up to a whole pack and inflated by the manager's ordering bias. Zero on days with no review or no trigger.
Ordered but not yet delivered.
True where demand could not be met in full from stock — the shortfall is a lost sale.
Surrogate key, one row per disposal event.
Day of disposal; joins to calendar.
Joins to ingredients.ingredient_id.
Who delivered the spoiled batch — spoilage attributes back to a supplier and its lead time.
Internal FEFO batch that spoiled. 0 for prep-trim, which is not tied to a single batch.
Quantity discarded, in the ingredient's uom.
Unit of measure: g, ml or pc.
expiry (aged past its effective shelf life), overstock (expired while holding well above normal usage), or prep-trim (unavoidable kitchen loss, 4-6% of throughput).
Cost of that batch, from the supplier's real unit rate plus its fluctuation band.
waste_quantity x unit_cost — the capital thrown away.
When the spoiled batch was delivered.
When it expired. Effective shelf life varies with batch quality and weather, so it is not simply received_date + shelf_life_days.
Days between receipt and disposal.
Surrogate key.
Real supplier name from the owner's SUPPLY-UR sheet.
What they supply, e.g. seafood/frozen.
Average days from order to delivery. Inflated by bad weather; capped below a perishable's shelf life, since it cannot outlive the trip.
Day-to-day variability in that lead time.
Share of orders delivered in full; the rest arrive short.
Minimum order the supplier accepts.
How often they run a delivery route.
Surrogate key.
Point-of-sale SKU. Not unique and not a key — 13 values are malformed and 6 items have 0. Join on item_id.
Dish name as printed on the menu. A few carry encoding corruption from the source export (e.g. 'Lemonadeuecea') and some near-duplicates differ only by spelling.
Menu section.
Menu price, taken from the owner's sales export.
Promotional item; year-stamped promos only sell in their own year.
Item used for management comps.
Currently on the menu.
First day it could be sold. Delivery-only items phase in during 2022.
Last day it could be sold. EMPTY ON EVERY ROW — nothing has been withdrawn from the menu yet.
Surrogate key.
The owner's recipe code, e.g. TUN, CF_060.
Product name cross-referenced from the purchasing catalogue.
Ingredient family: seafood, pork, veg, sauce, ...
ambient, chilled or frozen.
Unit of measure: g, ml or pc.
Grams in one portion, for portion-coded lines such as CF_060 (60 g chicken fillet). Empty for bulk lines.
Purchase pack, used to round orders up. Capped so a short-life line is not bought in quantities it cannot use.
Nominal shelf life (USDA FoodKeeper). Fish 1-2 d, leafy veg 3-7 d, frozen 60-180 d.
Subject to spoilage.
Cost per unit, from the owner's supplier rate sheet.
True where the code could not be matched to the catalogue and the name is a best guess — BAR, KAL and SAS only. Ask the owner before relying on these.
Dish; joins to menu_items.item_id.
Joins to ingredients.ingredient_id.
The owner's recipe code, for readability.
The owner's own recipe number, AS WRITTEN. Units are inconsistent in the source: portion-coded lines state portions, bulk lines state grams, though both are labelled g. Use qty_base for arithmetic.
qty_per_unit normalised to the ingredient's base unit (portions multiplied out by portion_g). This is what consumption is computed from.
Base unit the normalised quantity is expressed in.
Integer date key used by every fact table.
Day name, Monday to Sunday.
Day index, 0 = Monday. Wednesday (2) is the sales peak.
ISO week number.
Calendar month.
Calendar quarter.
Calendar year.
Saturday or Sunday. Note the trade peak is midweek, not at the weekend — this is an office district.
Philippine public holiday.
15th or month end, when spending lifts 8-15%.
September to December, the Philippine peak retail season.
